filter.description:
Subject filters. Ownership is always an additional backend-enforced
predicate and cannot be overridden by this filter.

Actor.description:
An opaque, transport-asserted caller identity.

Constructed by the transport after it authenticates the caller, relayed
verbatim by the kernel, and consumed only by plugins for data scoping. See
the [crate-level docs](crate) for the full contract.

claims.description:
Transport-asserted claims (e.g. `["admin"]`). Advisory only: the kernel
never branches on these. A plugin MAY consult them for its own
authorization decisions. Omitted from the wire when empty.

tenant_id.description:
Optional tenant / organization partition the user belongs to. Plugins
use it for multi-tenant data isolation. Omitted from the wire when
absent.

user_id.description:
Stable identifier for the authenticated user. Opaque to the kernel;
plugins use it to scope owned rows to a user.

SubjectFilter.description:
Filter passed to `subject/list`.

All fields are optional and combined with AND semantics. Empty `Vec`
fields mean "no constraint on this dimension". `cursor` is opaque to the
daemon — backends issue and accept their own pagination tokens.

assignee.description: Match subjects assigned to one of these identifiers.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor returned by a prior `subject/list` call.

dispatch_label.description:
Match subjects whose dispatch label (resolved by the backend from
its [`SubjectSchema::status_dispatch_hints`] table) equals this
value. Workflow YAML can use this to gate a phase on a label like
`"code-review"` without coupling to any one backend's vocabulary.

has_attachment_kind.description:
Match subjects that carry at least one [`SubjectAttachment`] whose
`kind` equals this value. Useful for `requires_document_attachment`
style gates.

kind.description: Match subjects whose `kind` is one of these.

labels_all.description: Match subjects that have all of these labels.

labels_any.description: Match subjects that have at least one of these labels.

limit.description: Suggested page size. Backends are free to clamp this.

native_status.description:
Match subjects whose backend-raw [`Subject::native_status`] equals
this value. Use when the normalized [`SubjectStatus`] is too coarse
— e.g. match Linear `"In Review"` but not `"In Progress"`, which
both map to [`SubjectStatus::InProgress`].

status.description: Match subjects whose status is one of these.

updated_since.description: Match subjects updated at or after this timestamp.

SubjectRequestContext.description:
Authenticated request context asserted by the application transport.

The actor is required on every v2 subject call. Correlation and
idempotency values are opaque transport identifiers: the kernel relays
them and the owning backend decides how to record or enforce them.

actor.description:
Authenticated caller. Claims remain advisory; ownership is the stable
`(user_id, tenant_id)` pair.

correlation_id.description: Optional correlation identifier spanning related requests.

idempotency_key.description: Optional idempotency key for a mutation.

request_id.description: Optional request identifier for tracing one transport request.

SubjectStatus.description:
Normalized cross-backend subject status.

Backend-native states (`"Backlog"`, `"In Review"`, `"Won't Fix"`, ...) map
into one of these five via the `status_map` declared per-subject in
workflow YAML. The mapping lives in configuration, not code, so adding a
new backend never requires extending this enum.

oneOf.description:
Currently being worked by a workflow run (or by a human, in the
upstream system).
